newsitem.title: CHINA: China paper slams U.S. "evil intentions" over HK.
newsitem.headline: China paper slams U.S. "evil intentions" over HK.

text.p: China's defence establishment on Tuesday fired a propaganda volley at the United States, saying hostile U.S. forces were determined to interfere in Hong Kong ahead of the British colony's return to Chinese rule.

Some people in the United States harboured "evil intentions" for Hong Kong as the territory prepared to mark the end of 156 years of colonial rule at midnight on June 30, warned a front-page headline in the official China Defence newspaper.

"Out of a need to maintain its global strategic position, the United States is strengthening its intelligence work in Hong Kong, supporting Hong Kong's Democratic Party and fostering political forces," the newspaper warned in a long editorial.
"Before and after Hong Kong's return, some U.S. politicians and intermediaries will certainly stir up trouble over the Hong Kong issue," it said.
"So-called 'democrats' within Hong Kong society will cooperate from afar with international forces hostile to China,' it said. "We must take precautions and then wait and see."
U.S. officials said on Monday that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would not attend the swearing-in of Beijing's controversial post-colonial legislature for the territory.
Albright plans to attend a ceremony to mark the formal handover, but not the inauguration of members of the provisional legislature that will replace Hong Kong's elected council.
China, which dismisses Western attacks on the provisional assembly's legitimacy, said attendance at both events would be optional.
Analysts say Hong Kong is likely to become a major irritant in a sensitive Sino-U.S. relaitionship already troubled by bitter disagreement over trade, human rights and Taiwan.
The China Defence article was the latest and one of the fiercest in a series of signals of Chinese frustration over Washington's policies on Hong Kong.
Beijing hails the return of Hong Kong as marking the end of more than 150 years of colonial humiliation and has promised a high degree of autonomy for the territory's 6.4 million people.

Many U.S. politicians, by contrast, have been more concerned by the effect on Hong Kong's political freedoms of its transfer to communist control and have angered Beijing by threatening economic penalties if liberties are rolled back.
Extensive U.S. commercial interests in Hong Kong meant Washington should work for a successful handover, but some politicians were trying to make trouble, China Defence warned.
"Over the last few years, some people in the United States have unceasingly spoken irresponsibly on the issue of Hong Kong and have carried out interference," the newspaper said.
"On the one hand they have stirred up trouble and spared no effort to encourage the British government and Hong Kong authorities to oppose the Chinese government," it said.
"On the other hand they have worked with the British to spread a pessimistic view of Hong Kong's prospects," it said.
Senior members of the U.S government had joined an anti-China wave by making indiscreet criticisms and bolstering Hong Kong pro-democracy activists, it said but named no names.

Western concerns over the future of Hong Kong have been fuelled by moves by China-backed future leader Tung Chee-hwa to limit the right to demonstrate and to restrict overseas funding for political groups.
The fierce foreign reaction to Tung's plans had unmasked an attempt by British authorities to make Hong Kong a place where anti-Chinese forces could act at will, China Defence said.
"This has made clear just in time that the timebomb buried by (the British Hong Kong authorities) must be dug out, otherwise Hong Kong will never find peace," it said.
